snippet.title: ₹70 Vs ₹3000 Biryani Battle in Delhi!! 🤯🍽️
snippet.description:
I spent the day trying three very different biryanis across Delhi, each at a completely different price point. From the busy lanes of Old Delhi to one of the city’s most iconic luxury kitchens, this tasting showed just how diverse Delhi’s biryani scene truly is. The contrast in techniques, textures and aromas made the journey even more fun.

The first stop was an unbelievable value discovery with rich rice and tender meat that delivered far more flavour than expected. The next plate, priced higher, offered soft buff, deeper spices and that satisfying feeling of getting your money’s worth. Both had their own charm and personality.

The final tasting was the legendary Dum Pukht experience at ITC Maurya where subtle aromas, beautifully cooked lamb and moist long-grain rice created a refined and memorable finish. Delhi really does have biryani for every craving.

snippet.title: Raan, Spice & Everything Nice | Mumbai’s Mughlai Icons | Khaana No. 1 Ep #36
snippet.description:
Welcome back to Khaana No. 1—where we chase the boldest flavors across the city. This time, we’re going big. Real big. We’re talking about Raan—the king of meats, the crown jewel of Mughlai feasts.

In this episode, we uncover three iconic spots in Mumbai that have turned this slow-cooked leg of lamb into a culinary legend. From smoky tandoori crusts to rich, masala-laced gravies—this is Raan like you’ve never seen it before.

🍖 In this episode:

Stop #1 – Persian Darbar 
📍Alexandra Terrace, Dr. B.A. Road, Byculla East, Mumbai 400027

Stop #2 – Delhi Zaika 
📍 250-A, Ground Floor, Darga Haji Musa Nakshbandi, Maulana Shaukat Ali Road, Grant Road, Mumbai 400008

Stop #3 – Shalimar Restaurant 
📍Vazir Building, Bhendi Bazaar, Near JJ Hospital, Mumbai 400003

What You’ll See: – Spice-laden gravies, and fall-off-the-bone lamb – Mughlai mastery, family feasts, and street-side royalty – The story of Raan: from royal courts to Mumbai’s bustling lanes

snippet.title: BEST BUTTER CHICKEN IN THE WORLD at LEGENDARY MOTI MAHAL RESTAURANT IN DARYAGANJ | बटर चिकन,दाल मखनी
snippet.description:
#butterchicken #foodie #food 
Don't Forget to Subscribe

MOTI MAHAL Restauranj
Address:- Daryaganj, New Delhi.

Butter Chicken: Yeh dish Moti Mahal ka dil hai! Creamy, tangy, aur mildly spicy, iska tomato-based gravy with tender chicken ek alag hi jadoo hai. Moti Mahal ne hi isse duniya ko diya, aur yeh ab global superstar hai. Thodi si makhani richness aur desi swad ka perfect balance—yeh sirf khana nahi, ek love story hai jo yahin se shuru hui!

Tandoori Chicken: Smoky, juicy, aur masaledar! Tandoor mein pakaya hua yeh chicken, yogurt aur spices ke marinade ke saath, ek char-grilled magic deta hai. Har bite mein crispy edges aur succulent meat ka maza—party ka hero!

Mutton Burra: Yeh hai mutton ka badshah! Spicy, succulent, aur tandoor mein perfectly charred, iske bold flavors aur tender texture aapko seedha Punjab ke dhabe pe le jayenge. Thoda wild, thoda intense—non-veg lovers ka ultimate crush!
Butter Chicken ko thoda alag isliye kehte hain kyunki yeh Moti Mahal ka original creation hai—ek aisa dish jo 1940s mein yahin paida hua aur aaj duniya bhar mein Indian cuisine ka naam roshan karta hai. Iska silky gravy aur mild flavors isse har kisi ka favorite banate hain, chahe woh desi ho ya videshi!

snippet.title: Delhi Street Food | Best Kachori In West Delhi | Zaika Riders
snippet.description:
Welcome to another exciting episode of Zaika Riders, where we dive deep into the vibrant world of Street Food in Delhi. In this vlog, we’re on a mission to discover some of the best street food in Delhi, and of course, we couldn't resist the allure of the iconic kachori in Delhi!

Our first stop takes us to the famous New Gopal Ji Poori Waale in Janakpuri, known for serving some of the most delicious kachori in Delhi. The crispy, golden kachoris paired with spicy aloo curry and tangy pickles make it a must-try for any food lover. If you’re ever in Janakpuri, you don’t want to miss this spot. Trust us, it's one of the best kachori joints in Delhi!

📍 Google Map Location - New Gopal Ji Poori Waale - Janakpuri
https://g.co/kgs/MDjBCK5

Next, we head to Brajwasi Ki Mashoor Kachori in H Block, Vikaspuri. This place is famous for its mouth-watering, perfectly fried kachoris, served with aloo sabzi. It’s no surprise that it’s called "mashoor" (famous) because their kachori stands out as one of the best in Delhi! If you’re craving a delicious, crispy kachori experience, this place is definitely worth the visit.

📍 Google Map Location - Brajwasi Ki Mashoor Kachori - Vikaspuri 
https://g.co/kgs/8agRq3w

snippet.title: Massive Baripada Evening Food Tour | Dahi Aalu + Guda Ladoo + Steamed Sandesh + Anda Tadka
snippet.description:
This episode is an immersive evening food tour in Baripada, led by our host Akash, a local who is deeply knowledgeable about the city’s heritage and culinary landscape.

We began our journey at Barik Tea Stall, fondly called BTS by locals, inspired by the Korean band due to its abbreviation. The coal oven here has a unique contraption that helps fan the fire efficiently. Akash has been coming here for the past 12 years. It is a popular spot for khatti, where people gather over tea and conversations. We also found a variety of cookies and snacks to go along with the tea.

Next, we visited Nini Bhai’s Dahi Aalu stall in Rathapadia, which has been around for nearly 40 years. Their signature dish, dahi aalu, is a tangy and comforting preparation of potatoes and curd with a perfect balance of spices. We also tried aalu dum, which was rich and flavourful, matar aalu kasa with its bold and spicy notes, and masala mudhi, a staple snack that is light, crunchy and deeply satisfying. Akash’s insights made the experience even richer.

We then headed to Jay Bajrang Guda Laddu, where we were joined by Mona. Here, we tried arisa pitha and the famous Baripada guda laddu. Guda laddu holds special significance as a key prasad during the Rath Yatra in Baripada. It has a unique texture with a slight caramelised sweetness, enhanced with subtle spices.

We made a short visit to the Baripada night market, which interestingly was once a Central Jail. From there, we went to Bapa Jhiya Jalakhia Dokan, a bustling fried snacks cart run by a father-daughter duo. We had masala mudhi and freshly fried chana dal fritters, which were crisp and flavourful. We also tried their special anda chop, a batter-coated egg snack topped with onions. It was a fun and indulgent evening bite.

Next, we stopped for some soda. The owner was warm and friendly, and we shared some great conversations filled with laughter. These small moments added so much warmth to the journey.

We then visited SSS Sweets to try their speciality, chhena poda. It was soft, caramelised and rich in flavour. We tried two variants and enjoyed both.

After this, we stopped at a crowded roadside anda ghugni stall. The ghugni topped with boiled eggs made for a wholesome and satisfying meal. The crowd itself spoke about its popularity.

Akash then took us to Babu Bhai’s shop to try punti kassa and other offal-based dishes. These are bold, masala-rich preparations and definitely an acquired taste. Locals love to enjoy them with mudhi.

Our next stop was Gajanan Vilas, known for its wide variety of sweets. We tried Mona ji’s favourite steamed sandesh and a malai roll. Both were light, fresh and delicately sweet.

We then visited Maguni Mixture, an old and famous namkeen shop that continues to draw huge crowds. We tried a few snacks and also got some packed. Both Akash and Mona have been coming here since childhood, which made it even more special.

Next, we headed to Kala Dhaba to try a unique combination of rice flour roti and country chicken kassa. It is a busy place and the rotis need to be pre-ordered as they are made in limited batches. The rotis were soft and paired beautifully with the rich, spicy chicken.

Our last stop for the day was Hotel Neelkamal. Here, we tried their anda tadka with mutton curry and a special chickpea-based starter. The flavours were bold, comforting and deeply satisfying. It is a favourite highway dhaba for many, and we could see why.

This evening in Baripada was not just about food. It was about people, stories, memories and discovering a city through its flavours. A heartfelt thank you to Akash and Mona for making this journey so special.

snippet.description:
This is a mini food vlog of my recent visit to Delhi’s famous Sarojini Nagar Market. Sarojini Nagar is one of the most famous markets in Delhi and it is well known for its variety of cheap clothes, jewellery, electronics and more. Although, other than shopping, Sarojini Nagar market is always famous for the delicious street food that is available at every corner of this market. The variety of street food items available in this market includes but is not limited to Momos, chaat, ice creams and fruits. Surprisingly, other than being an extremely cheap market for literally everything, Sarojini Nagar’s food was also extremely flavourful and unique in its own way. I had a great time visiting this market and trying out its food items. Hope you guys enjoy the video.

snippet.title: Old Delhi Street Food Tour | Purani Dilli ke Pakwaan | Ashok & Ashok Meat Dhaba|Bedmi Puri |Biryani
snippet.description:
Join Kunal Vijayakar in this mouth-watering episode of Khaane Mein Kya Hai, as he embarks on a flavorful journey through the heart of Old Delhi, discovering the city's iconic street food spots! From hidden gems to centuries-old food traditions, Kunal explores the best of Delhi’s street food culture.
Kunal kicks things off in Chandni Chowk, visiting Jain Pavitra Chach Bhandar for a comforting plate of homemade bread butter and a refreshing glass of chach.
- Next, he heads to Chawri Bazaar's Shyam Sweets to try their legendary Bedmi Puri with Aloo Sabzi — a must-try combo for all street food lovers.
- Kunal then takes a trip to Daulat Ki Chaat, an exquisite dessert that’s often compared to Malaiyo—a creamy, frothy delight that will leave you wanting more.
- Heading to Saddar Bazaar, Kunal indulges in the famous mutton and chicken preparations from Ashok & Ashok, a local favorite for tender, flavorful meats.
- To wrap things up, he makes his way to the historic Jama Masjid, where he tries the famous biryani prepared by none other than Kallan Bawarchi, a legendary name in Old Delhi’s biryani scene.

Don’t miss out on this gastronomic adventure through Old Delhi's narrow lanes and timeless flavors!
